label: Psychiatry
blurb: Antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilizers, anxiolytics, addiction

drugs.name: Fluoxetine
drugs.primaryEffect: Elevates mood and reduces anxiety over several weeks
drugs.treatmentUsage: Major depressive disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, bulimia nervosa, panic disorder, premenstrual dysphoric disorder
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selectively inhibits the presynaptic serotonin transporter, increasing serotonin in the synaptic cleft and eventually downregulating postsynaptic receptors.
drugs.sideEffects: Sexual dysfunction, nausea, insomnia, weight change, hyponatremia from SIADH, increased bleeding risk, serotonin syndrome, activation and suicidality in young patients
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent MAO inhibitors or use within five weeks of stopping fluoxetine, concurrent thioridazine or pimozide
drugs.tooltip: The longest half-life SSRI, so it rarely causes discontinuation syndrome but requires a five-week washout before starting an MAO inhibitor. First-line for OCD and bulimia.

drugs.name: Sertraline
drugs.primaryEffect: Improves mood and reduces anxiety symptoms
drugs.treatmentUsage: Major depressive disorder, panic disorder, PTSD, social anxiety disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Potently and selectively blocks the serotonin reuptake transporter, increasing synaptic serotonin availability.
drugs.sideEffects: Diarrhea (more than other SSRIs), sexual dysfunction, nausea, insomnia, hyponatremia, serotonin syndrome
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent MAO inhibitors or pimozide; caution in hepatic impairment
drugs.tooltip: Often the default first SSRI because of few drug interactions and safety in cardiac disease and pregnancy. Diarrhea is its most distinctive side effect relative to other SSRIs.

drugs.name: Paroxetine
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces depressive and anxiety symptoms with sedation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, PTSD
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Blocks the serotonin transporter with additional anticholinergic activity and potent CYP2D6 inhibition.
drugs.sideEffects: Sedation, weight gain, marked sexual dysfunction, anticholinergic effects, severe discontinuation syndrome, cardiac septal defects in first-trimester exposure
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy, concurrent MAO inhibitors, concurrent tamoxifen because CYP2D6 inhibition blocks its activation
drugs.tooltip: The SSRI to avoid in pregnancy because of cardiac defects, and the one with the worst discontinuation syndrome due to its short half-life. Potent CYP2D6 inhibition renders tamoxifen ineffective.

drugs.name: Escitalopram
drugs.primaryEffect: Improves mood with a favorable side effect profile
drugs.treatmentUsage: Major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder
drugs.mechanismOfAction: The active S-enantiomer of citalopram that selectively inhibits the serotonin transporter with high selectivity and minimal off-target activity.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea, insomnia, sexual dysfunction, QT prolongation at higher doses, hyponatremia
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent MAO inhibitors, congenital long QT syndrome
drugs.tooltip: The cleanest SSRI pharmacologically, with the fewest interactions. Dose-dependent QT prolongation is the reason its maximum dose is capped, especially in older adults.

drugs.name: Venlafaxine
drugs.primaryEffect: Improves mood and energy through serotonin and norepinephrine
drugs.treatmentUsage: Major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, neuropathic pain
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits serotonin reuptake at low doses and adds norepinephrine reuptake inhibition at higher doses, increasing both monoamines in the synapse.
drugs.sideEffects: Dose-dependent hypertension, nausea, sweating, insomnia, sexual dysfunction, severe discontinuation syndrome
drugs.contraindications: Uncontrolled hypertension, concurrent MAO inhibitors
drugs.tooltip: The dose-dependent hypertension is the classic teaching point: it is serotonergic at low dose and adds noradrenergic effect at higher dose. Blood pressure must be monitored.

drugs.name: Duloxetine
drugs.primaryEffect: Relieves depression and neuropathic pain simultaneously
drugs.treatmentUsage: Major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, fibromyalgia, chronic musculoskeletal pain, stress urinary incontinence
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Balanced inhibitor of serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake; the noradrenergic effect in descending spinal pathways produces analgesia independent of mood improvement.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea, dry mouth, constipation, hepatotoxicity, hypertension, sexual dysfunction, discontinuation syndrome
drugs.contraindications: Hepatic impairment, heavy alcohol use, narrow-angle glaucoma, concurrent MAO inhibitors
drugs.tooltip: The antidepressant to pick when depression coexists with diabetic neuropathy or fibromyalgia. Analgesia comes from descending noradrenergic inhibition, not from mood improvement.

drugs.name: Bupropion
drugs.primaryEffect: Improves mood and energy without sexual side effects
drugs.treatmentUsage: Major depressive disorder, seasonal affective disorder, smoking cessation, adjunct for SSRI-induced sexual dysfunction
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits reuptake of norepinephrine and dopamine with negligible serotonergic activity, and antagonizes nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.
drugs.sideEffects: Insomnia, agitation, dry mouth, headache, weight loss, seizures at high doses or in predisposed patients, hypertension
drugs.contraindications: Seizure disorder, bulimia or anorexia nervosa, abrupt alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal, concurrent MAO inhibitors
drugs.tooltip: The antidepressant of choice when sexual dysfunction or weight gain is unacceptable, since it causes neither. The lowered seizure threshold makes eating disorders an absolute contraindication.

drugs.name: Mirtazapine
drugs.primaryEffect: Improves mood while increasing appetite and sleep
drugs.treatmentUsage: Major depressive disorder, particularly with insomnia, poor appetite, or weight loss; depression in cancer and elderly patients
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Antagonizes presynaptic alpha-2 autoreceptors to increase norepinephrine and serotonin release, while blocking 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors and H1 histamine receptors.
drugs.sideEffects: Marked sedation, increased appetite and weight gain, dry mouth, dizziness, rare agranulocytosis, elevated cholesterol
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent MAO inhibitors; caution in obesity and metabolic syndrome
drugs.tooltip: Side effects are the reason to choose it: pick mirtazapine for the depressed elderly patient who cannot sleep and is losing weight. Sedation is paradoxically stronger at lower doses.

drugs.name: Trazodone
drugs.primaryEffect: Induces sleep at low dose and treats depression at high dose
drugs.treatmentUsage: Insomnia (most common use, at low doses), major depressive disorder at higher doses
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Blocks 5-HT2A receptors and weakly inhibits serotonin reuptake, with potent H1 and alpha-1 antagonism producing sedation.
drugs.sideEffects: Sedation, orthostatic hypotension, dry mouth, priapism (a urologic emergency), QT prolongation, serotonin syndrome
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent MAO inhibitors, recent myocardial infarction, known long QT syndrome
drugs.tooltip: Priapism is the classic board association and requires emergent urologic evaluation. Antidepressant doses are far higher than the 50 mg typically used for sleep.

drugs.name: Amitriptyline
drugs.primaryEffect: Relieves depression, neuropathic pain, and prevents migraine
drugs.treatmentUsage: Major depressive disorder, neuropathic pain, migraine prophylaxis, fibromyalgia, nocturnal enuresis in children
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits reuptake of serotonin and norepinephrine while also blocking muscarinic, histamine H1, and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors.
drugs.sideEffects: Sedation, anticholinergic effects, orthostatic hypotension, weight gain, QRS widening and arrhythmias in overdose, seizures, confusion in the elderly
drugs.contraindications: Recent myocardial infarction, arrhythmias, narrow-angle glaucoma, concurrent MAO inhibitors, elderly patients per Beers criteria
drugs.tooltip: Overdose is the classic emergency: the three Cs are Convulsions, Coma, and Cardiotoxicity with QRS widening. Treatment is sodium bicarbonate to overcome sodium channel blockade.

drugs.name: Nortriptyline
drugs.primaryEffect: Antidepressant and analgesic effect with less sedation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Major depressive disorder, neuropathic pain, smoking cessation; preferred tricyclic in older adults
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Secondary amine tricyclic that preferentially inhibits norepinephrine reuptake with fewer anticholinergic and antihistaminic effects than tertiary amines.
drugs.sideEffects: Dry mouth, constipation, orthostatic hypotension, sedation (less than amitriptyline), cardiac conduction delay in overdose
drugs.contraindications: Recent myocardial infarction, arrhythmias, concurrent MAO inhibitors, narrow-angle glaucoma
drugs.tooltip: The active metabolite of amitriptyline and the best tolerated tricyclic, which is why it is preferred in the elderly. It also has a well-defined therapeutic window that can be monitored.

drugs.name: Phenelzine
drugs.primaryEffect: Increases all monoamine neurotransmitters
drugs.treatmentUsage: Treatment-resistant depression, atypical depression with hypersomnia and hyperphagia, social anxiety disorder
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Irreversibly inhibits monoamine oxidase A and B, preventing degradation of serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine and raising their synaptic concentrations.
drugs.sideEffects: Hypertensive crisis with tyramine-containing foods, orthostatic hypotension, weight gain, sexual dysfunction, insomnia, serotonin syndrome
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics, meperidine, tramadol, dextromethorphan, or sympathomimetics; pheochromocytoma; tyramine-rich diet
drugs.tooltip: The cheese reaction: tyramine in aged cheese, cured meats, and wine displaces norepinephrine and causes hypertensive crisis. A two-week washout is required before switching to another antidepressant.

drugs.name: Haloperidol
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces positive psychotic symptoms and agitation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Schizophrenia, acute agitation and delirium, Tourette syndrome, intractable hiccups
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Potently antagonizes D2 dopamine receptors in the mesolimbic pathway, reducing hallucinations and delusions.
drugs.sideEffects: Extrapyramidal symptoms including acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, and tardive dyskinesia; neuroleptic malignant syndrome; hyperprolactinemia; QT prolongation
drugs.contraindications: Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, severe CNS depression, known long QT syndrome; boxed warning for mortality in elderly dementia patients
drugs.tooltip: High-potency typicals cause the most extrapyramidal symptoms and least anticholinergic effect. Timeline of EPS: hours for dystonia, days for akathisia, weeks for parkinsonism, months to years for tardive dyskinesia.

drugs.name: Chlorpromazine
drugs.primaryEffect: Antipsychotic effect with strong sedation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Schizophrenia, acute psychosis, intractable hiccups, severe nausea and vomiting
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Blocks D2 dopamine receptors along with substantial muscarinic, histamine H1, and alpha-1 adrenergic antagonism.
drugs.sideEffects: Sedation, orthostatic hypotension, anticholinergic effects, corneal and lens deposits, blue-gray skin discoloration, photosensitivity, cholestatic jaundice
drugs.contraindications: Severe CNS depression, narrow-angle glaucoma, dementia-related psychosis in the elderly
drugs.tooltip: Low potency means more anticholinergic, antihistamine, and alpha-blocking effects but fewer extrapyramidal symptoms. The unique clues are corneal deposits and blue-gray skin discoloration.

drugs.name: Risperidone
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces positive and negative psychotic symptoms
drugs.treatmentUsage: Schizophrenia, bipolar mania, irritability in autism spectrum disorder, adjunct in treatment-resistant depression
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Antagonizes D2 dopamine and 5-HT2A serotonin receptors; the serotonin blockade reduces extrapyramidal effects relative to typical antipsychotics.
drugs.sideEffects: Hyperprolactinemia with galactorrhea, gynecomastia, and amenorrhea; extrapyramidal symptoms at higher doses; weight gain; orthostatic hypotension; sedation
drugs.contraindications: Dementia-related psychosis in the elderly (boxed warning), prolactin-dependent tumors
drugs.tooltip: The atypical with the most hyperprolactinemia because it blocks D2 in the tuberoinfundibular pathway strongly. Classic vignette: a young man on risperidone develops gynecomastia.

drugs.name: Olanzapine
drugs.primaryEffect: Broad antipsychotic and mood-stabilizing effect
drugs.treatmentUsage: Schizophrenia, bipolar mania and maintenance, acute agitation, chemotherapy-induced nausea
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Antagonizes D2, 5-HT2A, histamine H1, and muscarinic receptors, producing antipsychotic effect with strong sedative and metabolic activity.
drugs.sideEffects: Substantial weight gain, dyslipidemia, new-onset type 2 diabetes and hyperglycemia, sedation, anticholinergic effects
drugs.contraindications: Dementia-related psychosis in the elderly (boxed warning); caution in metabolic syndrome and diabetes
drugs.tooltip: The worst metabolic offender among antipsychotics: weight gain, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes. Baseline and periodic weight, lipids, and glucose monitoring are mandatory.

drugs.name: Quetiapine
drugs.primaryEffect: Antipsychotic and mood stabilization with strong sedation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Schizophrenia, bipolar mania and bipolar depression, adjunct in major depression, psychosis in Parkinson disease
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Antagonizes D2 and 5-HT2A receptors with rapid D2 dissociation and potent H1 blockade; its metabolite norquetiapine inhibits norepinephrine reuptake.
drugs.sideEffects: Sedation, orthostatic hypotension, weight gain, dyslipidemia, cataracts, QT prolongation
drugs.contraindications: Dementia-related psychosis in the elderly (boxed warning), known long QT syndrome
drugs.tooltip: Its loose, rapidly dissociating D2 binding gives it the lowest extrapyramidal risk, which is why it is one of the few antipsychotics usable in Parkinson disease psychosis alongside pimavanserin and clozapine.

drugs.name: Clozapine
drugs.primaryEffect: Uniquely effective in treatment-resistant schizophrenia
drugs.treatmentUsage: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia after failure of two other antipsychotics; reduction of suicidality in schizophrenia
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Weak D2 antagonist with potent 5-HT2A, D4, muscarinic, histamine, and alpha-adrenergic antagonism; the precise basis of its superior efficacy remains unclear.
drugs.sideEffects: Agranulocytosis requiring absolute neutrophil count monitoring, myocarditis, seizures, severe sialorrhea, metabolic syndrome, orthostatic hypotension, ileus
drugs.contraindications: History of clozapine-induced agranulocytosis, severe neutropenia, uncontrolled seizure disorder, paralytic ileus
drugs.tooltip: The most effective antipsychotic and the most dangerous. Mandatory ANC monitoring for agranulocytosis. Paradoxical drooling despite anticholinergic activity, plus myocarditis and seizures, are the classic associations.

drugs.name: Aripiprazole
drugs.primaryEffect: Stabilizes dopamine signaling as a partial agonist
drugs.treatmentUsage: Schizophrenia, bipolar mania, adjunct for major depressive disorder, irritability in autism, Tourette syndrome
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Partial agonist at D2 and 5-HT1A receptors and antagonist at 5-HT2A, acting as a functional antagonist where dopamine is high and an agonist where it is low.
drugs.sideEffects: Akathisia (prominent), insomnia, nausea, headache, impulse control disorders including gambling, less weight gain than other atypicals
drugs.contraindications: Dementia-related psychosis in the elderly (boxed warning)
drugs.tooltip: The dopamine system stabilizer. Metabolically the most favorable atypical, but akathisia is common and impulse control disorders such as compulsive gambling are a recognized effect.

drugs.name: Lithium
drugs.primaryEffect: Stabilizes mood and reduces suicide risk in bipolar disorder
drugs.treatmentUsage: Bipolar disorder acute mania and maintenance; augmentation in treatment-resistant depression
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits inositol monophosphatase and glycogen synthase kinase-3, depleting inositol and altering second messenger signaling and neuronal excitability.
drugs.sideEffects: Tremor, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, hypothyroidism, weight gain, Ebstein anomaly in first-trimester exposure, chronic tubulointerstitial nephropathy, toxicity with ataxia and seizures
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy, significant renal impairment, sodium depletion or dehydration, concurrent NSAIDs, thiazides, or ACE inhibitors
drugs.tooltip: The only psychotropic proven to reduce suicide. Narrow therapeutic index with renal clearance means dehydration, NSAIDs, thiazides, and ACE inhibitors all precipitate toxicity. Monitor levels, thyroid, and kidney function.

drugs.name: Divalproex
drugs.primaryEffect: Controls acute mania and prevents mood episodes
drugs.treatmentUsage: Acute bipolar mania (especially mixed or rapid-cycling), bipolar maintenance, seizures, migraine prophylaxis
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Increases GABA levels by inhibiting GABA transaminase, blocks voltage-gated sodium channels, and inhibits histone deacetylase.
drugs.sideEffects: Weight gain, tremor, alopecia, thrombocytopenia, hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, hyperammonemia, polycystic ovary syndrome, severe teratogenicity
drugs.contraindications: Pregnancy (boxed warning), hepatic disease, urea cycle disorders, POLG mutations
drugs.tooltip: Preferred over lithium for mixed episodes and rapid cycling. Absolutely avoided in women of childbearing potential without contraception because of neural tube defects and reduced child IQ.

drugs.name: Carbamazepine (Psychiatric Use)
drugs.primaryEffect: Controls manic symptoms and stabilizes mood
drugs.treatmentUsage: Acute bipolar mania, bipolar maintenance in patients intolerant of lithium and valproate
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Blocks voltage-gated sodium channels and modulates neuronal excitability; it is also a potent inducer of multiple CYP450 enzymes including its own metabolism.
drugs.sideEffects: Agranulocytosis and aplastic anemia, SIADH with hyponatremia, ataxia, diplopia, Stevens-Johnson syndrome linked to HLA-B*1502, numerous drug interactions
drugs.contraindications: Bone marrow suppression, pregnancy, concurrent MAO inhibitors, HLA-B*1502 positive without careful consideration
drugs.tooltip: Its potent CYP induction causes oral contraceptive failure and reduces levels of many co-prescribed drugs, which is a favorite exam interaction. Also causes SIADH, in contrast to lithium causing diabetes insipidus.

drugs.name: Alprazolam
drugs.primaryEffect: Rapid relief of acute anxiety and panic
drugs.treatmentUsage: Panic disorder, short-term acute anxiety relief
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Binds the benzodiazepine site on GABA-A receptors and increases the frequency of chloride channel opening, potentiating GABA-mediated inhibition.
drugs.sideEffects: Sedation, cognitive impairment, anterograde amnesia, falls in the elderly, rapid tolerance and dependence, severe rebound anxiety and withdrawal seizures
drugs.contraindications: Substance use disorder, concurrent opioids, severe respiratory depression, narrow-angle glaucoma, pregnancy
drugs.tooltip: Short half-life and rapid onset make it both the most effective for acute panic and the most habit-forming. Withdrawal can cause seizures, so it must always be tapered rather than stopped.

drugs.name: Clonazepam
drugs.primaryEffect: Sustained anxiolysis and seizure suppression
drugs.treatmentUsage: Panic disorder, generalized anxiety, myoclonic and absence seizures, REM sleep behavior disorder, akathisia
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Enhances GABA-A receptor chloride channel opening frequency, increasing inhibitory neurotransmission throughout the central nervous system.
drugs.sideEffects: Sedation, ataxia, cognitive slowing, behavioral disinhibition in children, tolerance and dependence, withdrawal seizures
drugs.contraindications: Severe hepatic disease, acute narrow-angle glaucoma, concurrent opioids, significant respiratory depression
drugs.tooltip: Long half-life gives smoother coverage and less interdose rebound than alprazolam. First-line for REM sleep behavior disorder, which is a strong predictor of future synucleinopathy.

drugs.name: Buspirone
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces chronic anxiety without sedation or dependence
drugs.treatmentUsage: Generalized anxiety disorder, augmentation of antidepressants
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Partial agonist at presynaptic and postsynaptic 5-HT1A serotonin receptors, modulating serotonergic tone over weeks without acting on GABA.
drugs.sideEffects: Dizziness, headache, nausea, restlessness; no sedation, no respiratory depression, no dependence
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent MAO inhibitors; ineffective for acute anxiety or panic attacks
drugs.tooltip: The anxiolytic with no abuse potential, no sedation, and no withdrawal — ideal for patients with substance use history. The catch is that it takes one to two weeks to work and is useless as needed.

drugs.name: Zolpidem
drugs.primaryEffect: Induces sleep with minimal effect on sleep architecture
drugs.treatmentUsage: Short-term treatment of insomnia, particularly sleep-onset insomnia
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selectively binds the alpha-1 subunit-containing GABA-A receptor, producing sedation with relatively little anxiolytic, anticonvulsant, or muscle relaxant activity.
drugs.sideEffects: Complex sleep behaviors including sleepwalking, sleep-driving, and sleep-eating (boxed warning); next-day impairment; anterograde amnesia; falls in the elderly
drugs.contraindications: History of complex sleep behaviors on the drug, concurrent alcohol or opioids, severe hepatic impairment
drugs.tooltip: The Z-drugs bind selectively to alpha-1 GABA-A subunits, which is why they sedate without much anxiolysis. Boxed warning for complex sleep behaviors — a memorable vignette of a patient who cooked and ate while asleep.

drugs.name: Methylphenidate
drugs.primaryEffect: Improves attention, focus, and impulse control
drugs.treatmentUsage: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, narcolepsy
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Blocks the dopamine and norepinephrine transporters, increasing synaptic catecholamines in the prefrontal cortex and striatum.
drugs.sideEffects: Decreased appetite and weight loss, insomnia, growth suppression in children, tachycardia and hypertension, tics, irritability, abuse potential
drugs.contraindications: Structural cardiac abnormality or serious arrhythmia, concurrent MAO inhibitors, untreated hyperthyroidism, glaucoma
drugs.tooltip: First-line for ADHD along with amphetamines, and the most effective ADHD treatment. Appetite suppression, insomnia, and modest growth suppression are the expected effects to counsel about.

drugs.name: Amphetamine Salts
drugs.primaryEffect: Increases attention, wakefulness, and alertness
drugs.treatmentUsage: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, narcolepsy, binge eating disorder (lisdexamfetamine)
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Reverses the dopamine and norepinephrine transporters to drive catecholamine efflux and blocks VMAT2, releasing stored monoamines into the synapse.
drugs.sideEffects: Anorexia, insomnia, hypertension, tachycardia, psychosis at high doses, growth suppression, high abuse potential
drugs.contraindications: Structural cardiac disease, concurrent MAO inhibitors, substance use disorder, advanced arteriosclerosis, hyperthyroidism
drugs.tooltip: Amphetamines release stored catecholamines, whereas methylphenidate only blocks reuptake — that difference explains their higher potency and higher abuse liability.

drugs.name: Atomoxetine
drugs.primaryEffect: Improves attention without stimulant abuse potential
drugs.treatmentUsage: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, particularly with comorbid substance use, anxiety, or tics
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selectively inhibits the presynaptic norepinephrine transporter, which also raises dopamine in the prefrontal cortex where dopamine is cleared by that transporter.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea, decreased appetite, fatigue, hepatotoxicity, increased blood pressure and heart rate, suicidal ideation in adolescents (boxed warning)
drugs.contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma, pheochromocytoma, severe cardiovascular disease, concurrent MAO inhibitors
drugs.tooltip: The non-stimulant option, useful when abuse potential, tics, or anxiety make stimulants unwise. It takes several weeks to work rather than acting on the first dose.

drugs.name: Naltrexone
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces craving and reward from alcohol and opioids
drugs.treatmentUsage: Alcohol use disorder (first-line), opioid use disorder relapse prevention
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Competitively antagonizes mu opioid receptors, blocking the endogenous opioid-mediated reward that reinforces alcohol and opioid consumption.
drugs.sideEffects: Nausea, headache, hepatotoxicity at high doses, precipitated withdrawal in opioid-dependent patients, blocked analgesia from opioids
drugs.contraindications: Current opioid use or physiologic dependence, acute hepatitis or hepatic failure, anticipated need for opioid analgesia
drugs.tooltip: First-line for alcohol use disorder and available as a monthly injection. The patient must be opioid-free for 7 to 10 days first or it precipitates severe withdrawal.

drugs.name: Acamprosate
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces protracted withdrawal symptoms and craving
drugs.treatmentUsage: Maintenance of abstinence in alcohol use disorder after detoxification
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Modulates NMDA glutamate receptors and GABA signaling, restoring the excitatory-inhibitory balance disrupted by chronic alcohol exposure.
drugs.sideEffects: Diarrhea, nausea, anxiety, depression, rare suicidal ideation
drugs.contraindications: Severe renal impairment with creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min
drugs.tooltip: Renally cleared and not hepatically metabolized, which makes it the preferred agent for alcohol use disorder in patients with liver disease where naltrexone is risky.

drugs.name: Disulfiram
drugs.primaryEffect: Creates a severe aversive reaction to alcohol
drugs.treatmentUsage: Alcohol use disorder in highly motivated patients with supervised administration
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Irreversibly inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase, causing acetaldehyde to accumulate after alcohol ingestion and produce flushing, nausea, and tachycardia.
drugs.sideEffects: Severe flushing, vomiting, headache, hypotension, and tachycardia with alcohol; hepatotoxicity, peripheral neuropathy, psychosis
drugs.contraindications: Recent alcohol ingestion within 12 hours, severe cardiac disease, psychosis, concurrent metronidazole, pregnancy
drugs.tooltip: Purely aversive — it does nothing for craving. Patients must avoid hidden alcohol in mouthwash, cough syrup, and sauces. Metronidazole and certain cephalosporins cause the same reaction.

drugs.name: Buprenorphine / Naloxone
drugs.primaryEffect: Suppresses opioid withdrawal and craving with a ceiling on respiratory depression
drugs.treatmentUsage: Opioid use disorder maintenance therapy; chronic pain in selected patients
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Buprenorphine is a high-affinity partial mu agonist that occupies receptors without full activation; naloxone is added to deter injection since it is inactive orally.
drugs.sideEffects: Constipation, sedation, headache, precipitated withdrawal if given too soon after a full agonist, QT prolongation, hepatotoxicity
drugs.contraindications: Current intoxication with full opioid agonists, severe respiratory compromise, severe hepatic impairment
drugs.tooltip: The ceiling effect on respiratory depression makes it far safer than methadone and prescribable in the office. Its high receptor affinity means it displaces full agonists and precipitates withdrawal if started too early.

drugs.name: Methadone
drugs.primaryEffect: Prevents opioid withdrawal and blocks euphoria from other opioids
drugs.treatmentUsage: Opioid use disorder maintenance in a licensed program; chronic and cancer pain
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Long-acting full mu opioid receptor agonist with additional NMDA receptor antagonism, providing stable receptor occupancy over 24 hours.
drugs.sideEffects: Respiratory depression, QT prolongation and torsades de pointes, constipation, sedation, hypogonadism, accumulation with unpredictable half-life
drugs.contraindications: Significant respiratory depression, paralytic ileus, concurrent QT-prolonging drugs without monitoring, long QT syndrome
drugs.tooltip: Highly effective but dangerous during initiation because its analgesic duration is much shorter than its elimination half-life, so it accumulates. QT prolongation requires baseline and follow-up ECGs.

drugs.name: Naloxone
drugs.primaryEffect: Immediately reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression
drugs.treatmentUsage: Acute opioid overdose; take-home harm reduction kits
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Competitive antagonist with high affinity at mu opioid receptors, rapidly displacing agonists and restoring respiratory drive.
drugs.sideEffects: Acute opioid withdrawal with agitation, vomiting, tachycardia, and hypertension; pulmonary edema; recurrence of overdose when it wears off
drugs.contraindications: None in a true overdose emergency; caution because its duration may be shorter than that of the opioid ingested
drugs.tooltip: Duration is 30 to 90 minutes, often shorter than the opioid it reverses, so patients must be observed for re-sedation. Repeat dosing or an infusion may be required for long-acting opioids.

drugs.name: Flumazenil
drugs.primaryEffect: Reverses benzodiazepine-induced sedation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Reversal of procedural sedation with benzodiazepines; rarely, isolated benzodiazepine overdose
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Competitive antagonist at the benzodiazepine binding site of the GABA-A receptor, displacing benzodiazepines and reversing their potentiation of GABA.
drugs.sideEffects: Precipitated withdrawal seizures in benzodiazepine-dependent patients, agitation, arrhythmias, resedation as it wears off
drugs.contraindications: Chronic benzodiazepine dependence, suspected tricyclic antidepressant co-ingestion, known seizure disorder
drugs.tooltip: Rarely used in overdose because it can precipitate refractory seizures in dependent patients or those who co-ingested tricyclics. Supportive care is usually preferred over reversal.

drugs.name: Hydroxyzine
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces anxiety and pruritus with sedation
drugs.treatmentUsage: Short-term anxiety relief, pruritus, insomnia, preoperative sedation, adjunct in alcohol withdrawal
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Antagonizes central H1 histamine receptors and has 5-HT2A antagonist activity, producing anxiolysis and sedation without GABAergic dependence.
drugs.sideEffects: Sedation, dry mouth, dizziness, QT prolongation at high doses, confusion in the elderly
drugs.contraindications: Prolonged QT interval, narrow-angle glaucoma, early pregnancy, elderly patients per Beers criteria
drugs.tooltip: A useful as-needed anxiolytic with no abuse potential, which makes it valuable in patients with substance use disorder where benzodiazepines are inappropriate.

drugs.name: Prazosin
drugs.primaryEffect: Reduces trauma-related nightmares and improves sleep
drugs.treatmentUsage: PTSD-associated nightmares and sleep disturbance; hypertension; benign prostatic hyperplasia
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Selectively blocks alpha-1 adrenergic receptors, reducing central noradrenergic activity during sleep that drives nightmare generation in PTSD.
drugs.sideEffects: First-dose orthostatic hypotension and syncope, dizziness, headache, nasal congestion, priapism rarely
drugs.contraindications: Hypotension, concurrent PDE5 inhibitors without careful timing
drugs.tooltip: The go-to for PTSD nightmares. The first-dose phenomenon means the initial dose is given at bedtime and titrated slowly to avoid syncope.

drugs.name: Esketamine
drugs.primaryEffect: Produces rapid antidepressant response within hours
drugs.treatmentUsage: Treatment-resistant depression and depression with acute suicidal ideation, given with an oral antidepressant
drugs.mechanismOfAction: The S-enantiomer of ketamine, a noncompetitive NMDA receptor antagonist that triggers a glutamate surge and rapid synaptogenesis through AMPA receptor and mTOR signaling.
drugs.sideEffects: Dissociation, sedation, dizziness, nausea, transient hypertension, abuse potential, bladder toxicity with chronic use
drugs.contraindications: Aneurysmal vascular disease, intracerebral hemorrhage history, hypersensitivity; requires administration under supervision
drugs.tooltip: The first fundamentally new antidepressant mechanism in decades, working in hours rather than weeks. Given as a nasal spray under two hours of clinical monitoring in a certified setting.

drugs.name: Lurasidone
drugs.primaryEffect: Treats bipolar depression with a favorable metabolic profile
drugs.treatmentUsage: Bipolar I depression, schizophrenia
drugs.mechanismOfAction: Antagonizes D2 and 5-HT2A receptors and acts as a 5-HT7 antagonist and 5-HT1A partial agonist, which may underlie its antidepressant effect.
drugs.sideEffects: Akathisia, somnolence, nausea, parkinsonism; minimal weight gain and metabolic disturbance
drugs.contraindications: Concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers, dementia-related psychosis in the elderly
drugs.tooltip: One of the few agents approved for bipolar depression, with far less weight gain than olanzapine or quetiapine. It must be taken with at least 350 calories of food for adequate absorption.
